messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT [P1] GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTED - cluster=prod-gpu - queue growth high, paging oncall @alex :rotating_light:

alex: got the page. seeing enqueue spike from inference-q, backlog ~11.7k, avg wait ~220s. 429s increasing for low-priority jobs.

maya: joining. oncall handoff in 8m if you need me to take. which nodegroup is starving?

alex: looks like nodegroup gpu-nodes-2. cluster-autoscaler logs: 'Failed to scale up: LaunchTemplate/InstanceProfile error' and k8s events show repeated 'NoCapacity' and 'FailedCreatePodSandBox' for gpu pods.

sam: link to autoscaler events: https://k8s-logs/prod/gpu/autoscaler — tons of "launch template does not reference an instance profile" entries. ASG 'gpu-nodes-2-asg' desired=2, max=6 but new instances not launching.

jules: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` -> only 2 gpu nodes, both fully utilized. Pending pods: 5,200, many in inference worker class.

alex: cluster-autoscaler: `failed to find compatible launch template -> AccessDenied: ec2:RunInstances` in cloudtrail. probable IAM role/instance-profile mismatch on the launch template.

infra-bot: CloudTrail event: "ec2:RunInstances" denied for LT:lt-0abcd1234 because instance profile 'redwood-prod-gpu-role' not associated with LT. Also ASG attempted to use obsolete LT version.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) manually create a healthy GPU node to relieve backlog 2) bump ASG desired to force scale while we fix LT/iam 3) route non-critical jobs to cpu-pool fallback 4)remove strict taints that block kube-system add-ons from scheduling on newly created nodes (if needed).

maya: ok i'll take step 2/3. sam can you start step 1 (manual instance) with the correct instance profile?

sam: on it. running the run-instances with correct IAM profile and tags so it joins autoscaling group via node registration:
```
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0gpufriend --instance-type p3.2xlarge \
  --iam-instance-profile Name=redwood-prod-gpu-role \
  --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=kubernetes.io/cluster/prod,Value=owned},{Key=redwood:role,Value=gpu-fallback}]'
```

jules: i'm patching the router to send low-priority inference to cpu-pool and increasing timeout for retries. small traffic shift will drop cost but reduce queue growth.

alex: updating ASG desired now: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-nodes-2-asg --desired-capacity 4` — will post output.

ops-bot: ASG update initiated for gpu-nodes-2-asg, desired -> 4 (requested by alex).

infra-bot: also noticed launch template version in ASG is lt-version 1 which references instance-profile that no longer exists. Suggest patch LT to use iamInstanceProfile 'redwood-prod-gpu-role' and bump template version.

sam: manual instance booting, cloud-init logs show kubelet registering but taint application failing because the launch template had node-labels that include `nvidia.com/gpu: present` but the bootstrap script attempts to apply `nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule` and then fails due to missing permissions in node bootstrap to write tags. workaround: i'll skip taint on bootstrap so kube-system can schedule critical pods.

alex: if you can skip taint we can get schedulables quicker. command to remove taint if applied: `kubectl taint nodes <node-name> nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule-`

sam: node joined: ip=10.2.45.18, kubelet registered, kube-proxy + node-exporter up. not seeing the taint applied now. pods started to land.

jules: after router change + one manual node, queue growth rate dropped ~60%. pending now 6,400 -> 3,200 in 7m.

alex: ASG scaling didn't spawn because of LT issue, but manual node helped. i'm going to patch the launch template to attach correct instance profile and update ASG to use new version. Doing `aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id lt-0abcd1234 --default-version 3 --launch-template-name gpu-lt`

infra-bot: note: modifying LT will not retroactively fix already attempted launches; ASG needs to be told to use the new version (set LaunchTemplateSpecification.Version to the new version or call `update-auto-scaling-group` with `--launch-template` param).

maya: i'll take the oncall. alex, handover when you're ready. provide summary for pgp handoff: cause = launch template/iam mismatch preventing autoscaler ASG from launching nodes, symptoms = queue growth, 429 throttles, partial customer impact.

alex: handing off to @maya. current status: manual node(s) up (2 added), ASG desired set to 4 but ASG failed to launch new instances until LT patched. i've updated LT to version 3 referencing instance-profile redwood-prod-gpu-role and triggered ASG to use it.

ops-bot: ASG event: Launch template version updated, starting instance launches.

jules: new nodes coming up (2 more initializing). pending pods decreasing: 3,200 -> 900 in 10m. 429 errors reduced to <10/min for affected customers.

maya: good. customer-impact note: 3 high-volume customers saw degraded throughput for ~28m peak impact window. we notified CS and opened incident notification.

alex: followups to create postmortem: 1) ensure LT has CI check for instance-profile drift 2) add autoscaler health check that alerts when ASG attempts failed due to permissions 3) create runbook for manual temp node creation and safe taint rollback 4) short-term: bump ASG min to 2 from 0 for gpu-nodes-2. 5) longer-term: make launch-template immutable with required iamProfile tag.

maya: assigning postmortem owner to alex. i'll file the incident and set RFC for LT validation.

infra-bot: resolution we saw: LT version change + manual node boot + router fallback drained queue. incident status -> mitigated.

alex: thanks everyone. will follow up with timeline and RCA in incidents/postmortems.

maya: closing handoff: oncall clear for now, reopening if we see >5% 429s or queue growth >1k/min.

ops-bot: Incident mitigated. Creating incident ticket IR-2026-0314-001 and adding notes.
